articles.title: Bioorthogonal chemistry conjugates: ADCs and beyond.
articles.abstract: Bioorthogonal click chemistry has played a transformative role in developing advanced hybrid conjugates. These molecular constructs are formed by chemically linking a targeting component to a functional moiety through a suitable linker. Therapeutic conjugates are designed to deliver a biologically active agent to a specific target to treat, prevent, or modify a disease process. By directing the payload to a defined site of action, these conjugates can improve efficacy while reducing off-target effects and systemic toxicity. Among these, antibody-drug conjugates stand out as the most clinically successful compounds. Where various chemical strategies, such as thiol-maleimide additions and site-selective glycan engineering, are employed to attach toxic payloads to antibodies with high precision and reduced sample heterogeneity. Beyond delivery of potent therapeutic payloads, click chemistry approaches have expanded into radioimmunoconjugates for diagnostics, oligonucleotide conjugates for gene silencing, and the creation of bispecific antibodies that can target multiple disease pathways simultaneously. These modular approaches often utilize combinations of ligation and chemical conjugation to preserve the structural integrity and immune functions of the original proteins. These techniques are now being applied to modulate living systems, including cell surface engineering, where metabolic machinery is exploited to install chemical handles on living cells for therapeutic tracking and "click-to-release" drug activation in vivo. Ultimately, current and emerging molecular "click" technologies emphasize a shift toward homogeneous, site-specific methods that expand the functionality and improve the stability, efficacy, and clinical potential of diverse bioconjugates to enhance the precision of modern medicine.

articles.title: Structural insights into P-glycoprotein substrate polyspecificity: A dynamic conformational sampling model.
articles.abstract: P-glycoprotein (P-gp, also known as ABCB1) is a member of the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter family that protects tissues from diverse xenobiotics and contributes to multidrug resistance in cancer. Despite extensive structural, biochemical, and biophysical studies, the molecular basis of its remarkable substrate polyspecificity remains incompletely understood. Recent structures of P-gp and its homologs, including zebrafish Abcb4, have revealed extensive conformational heterogeneity and provided unprecedented views of substrate and inhibitor recognition. In this review, we integrate structural and functional studies to examine how conformational variability of the drug-binding site contributes to P-gp polyspecificity. We highlight the continuum of inward-facing conformations and the coupling between local changes in drug-binding site architecture, including transmembrane-helix rotation and tilting, and the global opening and closing of the transporter's two pseudo-symmetric halves. We propose a dynamic conformational sampling model in which diverse substrates can recognize and possibly stabilize different conformational states of P-gp and, in some cases, adopt distinct binding poses. We further discuss how this dynamic view provides a framework for understanding the complex pharmacological behavior of P-gp and may inform the development of more effective inhibitors.

articles.title: Mechanistic benchmarking of SNAC, DDM, and LLC reveals enhancer-dependent pathways for intestinal semaglutide delivery.
articles.abstract: The oral delivery of peptide therapeutics remains constrained by poor intestinal permeability and the challenge of enhancing epithelial transport without compromising mucosal integrity. Although sodium N-(8-[2-hydroxybenzoyl]amino) caprylate (SNAC) enables gastric absorption of oral semaglutide and has also been explored for small-intestinal absorption of other peptide drugs, its suitability for enteric intestinal delivery of semaglutide remains unexplored. Here, we performed a comparative mechanistic evaluation of three permeation enhancers (SNAC, N-dodecyl-β-D-maltoside, and lauroyl-l-carnitine) for enteric delivery of semaglutide. Mechanisms were screened in epithelial monolayers and in situ intestinal absorption in rats, and the enhancers carried forward were formulated into enteric-coated capsules and evaluated in beagle dogs, with the leading candidate taken in to cynomolgus monkeys. In differentiated Caco-2 monolayers, all enhancers increased semaglutide transport but exhibited distinct transport mechanisms and barrier-response profiles. SNAC increased permeability without increasing mannitol transport or disrupting ZO-1, indicating a largely non-paracellular, cargo-dependent profile. DDM markedly increased paracellular marker transport and disrupted tight-junction organization, consistent with a primarily paracellular mode of action associated with reduced barrier recoverability. LLC showed a more favorable balance between transport enhancement and barrier recovery, while also increasing intracellular semaglutide-associated fluorescence and FD4 permeability. Rab5 immunostaining and dynasore inhibition indicated a dynamin-sensitive uptake component alongside partial tight-junction modulation. In rats, LLC produced the greatest increase in semaglutide absorption, and this effect was substantially attenuated by dynasore co-treatment. Transmission electron microscopy and tissue immunofluorescence further supported the presence of LLC-associated micelle-like structures, Rab5-related intracellular trafficking and junctional remodelling, with no overt tissue injury on local or systemic histology. For large-animal translation, citric acid and L-arginine improved semaglutide stability in intestinal fluids, and the resulting LLC-containing enteric formulation markedly increased systemic exposure in orally dosed beagle dogs and in cynomolgus monkeys following intraduodenal delivery. Collectively, these findings identify LLC as a promising permeation enhancer within the present SNAC/DDM/LLC comparison for enteric intestinal delivery of semaglutide and highlight how coordinated uptake-related and barrier-modulating mechanisms can support intestinal semaglutide absorption.

articles.title: Interaction with NEGR1 affects mGlu5 cell signalling and the neuroprotection induced by the positive allosteric modulator VU0409551.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The metabotropic glutamate receptor mGlu5 plays an important role in neuronal survival and synaptic plasticity. We and others have shown that mGlu5 positive allosteric modulators (PAMs) are biased agonists, triggering the activation of neuroprotective pathways and promoting neuronal survival. As mGlu5 biased pharmacology arises from drug-induced interactions with different protein partners, in this study, we analysed the mGlu5 interactome to identify novel binding partners capable of modulating receptor cell signalling. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: To identify new mGlu5 partners, we employed mass spectrometry, followed by co-immunoprecipitation experiments, which confirmed the interaction between mGlu5 and the neuronal growth regulator 1 (NEGR1), a cell adhesion molecule. We next evaluated how NEGR1 affects mGlu5 cell signalling and cellular distribution using lentivirus transduction on primary neuronal cultures to knockdown NEGR1 expression. We also assessed whether NEGR1 plays a role in the neuroprotective effects of the mGlu5 PAM, VU0409551, by evaluating apoptotic cell death and neurite degeneration. KEY RESULTS: The interaction between NEGR1 and mGlu5 is important for mGlu5 synaptic localization and for its coupling with Homer, thereby modulating cell signalling pathways activated by mGlu5 receptors. For instance, NEGR1 knockdown led to decreased mGlu5-dependent activation of ERK1/2 and reduced expression of ARC/ARG3.1 and BDNF. Importantly, NEGR1 knockdown affected mGlu5 pharmacology, as the neuroprotective effect of VU0409551 was not observed in neurons expressing low levels of NEGR1. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: These results indicate that NEGR1 is essential for mGlu5-biased activation of neuroprotective cell signalling pathways and for the neuroprotective effects triggered by VU0409551.

articles.title: Nationwide dalbavancin surveillance identifies sagB-associated cell-wall adaptation linked to reduced lipoglycopeptide susceptibility in CC5 Staphylococcus aureus.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Dalbavancin is a long-acting lipoglycopeptide with potent activity against Staphylococcus aureus. However, the emergence of reduced dalbavancin susceptibility and its underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. METHODS: Dalbavancin MICs were determined for 1803 S. aureus isolates from 37 hospitals in 27 provinces of China. Comparative genomics of a clinical dalbavancin-nonsusceptible (DAL-NS) isolate and in vitro vancomycin-selected derivatives was performed to identify resistance-associated mutations. The role of sagB was assessed by gene deletion and complementation, followed by antimicrobial susceptibility testing and phenotypic assays. Transcriptomic profiling, autolysis assays, electron microscopy, cytochrome c binding assays, and time-kill assays were performed to characterize the cellular effects of sagB dysfunction. RESULTS: Dalbavancin showed potent activity, with MIC50/MIC90 values of 0.06/0.125 μg/mL, and only one nonsusceptible isolate was detected (0.06%, 1/1803). This isolate belonged to ST5523/CC5 and had prior vancomycin exposure but no dalbavancin treatment. sagB mutations occurred in both the clinical isolate and independent vancomycin-selected derivatives with reduced dalbavancin susceptibility. Genetic complementation and deletion supported sagB dysfunction as contributing to reduced susceptibility to lipoglycopeptides, glycopeptides, and lipopeptides, with reciprocal β-lactam sensitization. Mechanistically, sagB dysfunction altered cell-wall hydrolase expression, autolysis, and envelope properties, and was associated with prolonged survival under dalbavancin exposure but enhanced killing by oxacillin. CONCLUSIONS: Dalbavancin remains highly active against clinical S. aureus in China. Rare nonsusceptibility may emerge under glycopeptide pressure through lineage-conditioned sagB-associated cell-wall remodeling.

articles.title: A Pilot Randomized Study of NAT2 and YEATS4 Pharmacogenetic Return of Results in Adults with Hypertension and African Ancestry: The GUARDD-US PGx Study.
articles.abstract: Almost half of individuals with hypertension fail to achieve recommended blood pressure (BP) goals. Pharmacogenetic gene-drug interactions may alter the efficacy of antihypertensive agents. We conducted a multicenter randomized controlled sub-study of participants (N = 1874) with hypertension and self-reported African ancestry to determine whether pharmacogenetic return of results (RoR) would improve systolic blood pressure (SBP) at 3 months. Participants were randomized to immediate pharmacogenetic RoR (intervention) or delayed RoR at trial completion (control). Clinical decision support conveyed recommendations for YEATS4-guided thiazide diuretic selection and NAT2-guided hydralazine dosing. Prespecified subgroup analyses included those with uncontrolled BP (baseline SBP ≥140 or DBP ≥90 mm Hg) and actionable genotypes. Immediate RoR did not improve SBP at 3 months in a broad population of hypertensive adults with controlled and uncontrolled SBP (covariate-adjusted change in SBP between groups: -0.3 ± 0.74 mm Hg, 95% CI: -1.8, 1.2). In participants with an actionable YEATS4 genotype (N = 867) predicting reduced thiazide efficacy, immediate RoR led to greater SBP reduction at 3 months (-2.46 mm Hg, 95% CI: -4.57 to -0.36). In participants with uncontrolled hypertension at baseline (N = 659), immediate RoR led to a greater reduction in SBP (-2.9 ± 0.74 mm Hg, 95% CI: -5.6, -0.3). Although no SBP reduction was observed in the whole cohort, participants with an actionable YEATS4 genotype or uncontrolled BP who received immediate RoR had a significantly greater SBP improvement than those with delayed RoR. Future studies of antihypertensive pharmacogenetics should recruit individuals with uncontrolled BP and actionable genotypes.

articles.title: Advances and challenges in inner ear drug delivery: limitations and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Hearing loss is a major global health burden, with age-related hearing loss affecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide. Despite significant therapeutic advances, effective treatment remains hampered by the challenge of delivering drugs to the inner ear, an anatomically inaccessible and tightly protected organ. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review was based on an extensive search of major biomedical databases and focuses on the anatomical and physiological barriers that limit inner ear drug delivery, current and emerging administration routes, and advanced delivery systems, including hydrogels, nanoparticles, microdevices and implantable platforms. Particular attention is given to the factors governing nanocarrier performance and to the key challenges for clinical translation, such as species-dependent pharmacokinetics, manufacturing reproducibility, GMP-compatible scale-up and regulatory requirements. Studies published between 2001 and 2026 were identified through PubMed, Embase, Web of Science and ClinicalTrials.gov. EXPERT OPINION: Despite rapid preclinical innovation, clinical translation remains uneven. Systemic sodium thiosulfate provides the strongest regulatory proof of clinically meaningful otoprotection, whereas recent intracochlear gene therapy establishes an important benchmark for localized treatment. For nanomedicine, progress will depend less on platform novelty than on rational structure-property design, reproducible cochlear exposure, cell-resolved biodistribution, large-animal validation, GMP-compatible manufacturing, patient stratification and clinical trial design.

articles.title: Should mitochondrial membrane potential be reconsidered as a criterion of cell death?
The unfolded protein response as a proteotoxic stress-resolution circuit: branch-selective signaling and failed resolution in environmental immunotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Environmental immunotoxicity is commonly framed through oxidative stress, cytotoxicity, inflammation, receptor-mediated signaling and cell- or tissue-specific mechanisms. This review proposes that proteotoxic stress resolution represents an additional layer linking environmental exposure to immune dysfunction. Specifically, the unfolded protein response (UPR) is considered as a branch-selective proteotoxic stress-resolution circuit that can shape immune outcomes when endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis is perturbed. The framework is offered as a hypothesis-generating conceptual structure rather than an established mechanistic paradigm, and the causal step linking failed resolution to immune dysfunction remains largely extrapolated from non-toxicological ER-stress models. Evidence from ER proteostasis biology, immune-cell function and toxicology indicates that environmental toxicants can disrupt protein folding, ER calcium balance, redox homeostasis, lipid composition, degradation pathways and secretory load, thereby engaging distinct combinations of IRE1α, PERK and ATF6 signaling. These branches generate immune-relevant outputs: IRE1α links ER stress to RNA processing and inflammatory signaling, PERK controls translational suppression and fate selection, and ATF6 supports restoration of folding capacity and secretory competence. Across macrophages, dendritic cells, T cells, plasma cells and barrier epithelial cells, immune outcomes depend on branch bias, signaling duration, cell-type context and resolution through ER-associated degradation, autophagy, ER-phagy, translational recovery and restoration of calcium and redox balance. This framework predicts that repeated low-dose exposures, mixed toxicant inputs and incomplete post-exposure recovery can shift immune or barrier cells into inflammatory, suppressive or barrier-disruptive states without overt cytotoxicity. It also supports time-resolved, branch-specific and cell-specific profiling for immunotoxic risk assessment.

articles.title: Integrating emerging preservation strategies in cardiac transplantation: From nanotherapeutic frontiers to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Hypothermic preservation remains a critical bottleneck in heart transplantation, primarily due to the exacerbation of ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and tightly restricted organ viability windows. Addressing this global clinical crisis requires a departure from traditional monotherapies. This review critically appraises-rather than merely synthesizes-three multidisciplinary advancements: (1) preservation solutions supplemented with nanotherapeutics, with explicit distinction between proof-of-concept, small-animal, and clinically translatable evidence; (2) technological transitions from static cold storage (SCS) to ex vivo heart perfusion (EVHP) and nanowarming-assisted cryopreservation; and (3) bioactive compounds derived from Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), evaluated through a SWOT framework that acknowledges phytochemical variability and the paucity of clinical transplantation data. We further examine the emerging-but currently nascent and largely speculative---role of artificial intelligence in perfusion decision support. We emphasize that these three domains are not evidentially equivalent: perfusion technology is clinically implemented, pharmacological and nanotherapeutic adjuncts remain predominantly preclinical, and AI applications in cardiac preservation are currently confined to retrospective outcome modelling, with no published closed-loop perfusion control in clinical practice.

articles.title: Microneedle-based drug delivery for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases: current applications and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases encompass a spectrum of conditions that arise from dysregulated immune-inflammatory responses marked by a chronic clinical course, a propensity for relapse, and a tendency to cause significant ocular tissue damage, which can lead to profound impairment of visual function. Dysregulation of the balance between immune cell subpopulations is central to the pathogenesis of many of these diseases. At present, non-specific treatments such as glucocorticoids and immunosuppressants form the cornerstone of therapy for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases. However, these treatments often suffer from poor bioavailability and targeting, cumbersome or invasive administration methods, and are associated with side effects such as increased intraocular pressure (IOP), cataracts, or glaucoma with frequent administration. These limitations underscore the urgent need for alternative drug delivery methods. Microneedles have emerged as an innovative approach to ocular drug delivery, offering distinct advantages over traditional eye drops and intravitreal injections. They enhance drug penetration and targeting, provide sustained release, and may reduce unnecessary drug exposure, thus holding great promise for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases. This review aims to shed light on the unique benefits and efficacy of microneedles as drug-delivery systems for inflammatory and immune-mediated ocular diseases, with particular attention to noninfectious uveitis, corneal inflammatory disorders, inflammation-associated corneal neovascularization, and allergic conjunctivitis. It also discusses ocular safety and toxicity, manufacturing and standardization, regulatory challenges, and future prospects of microneedle applications, providing a comprehensive overview of their potential for ocular drug delivery.

articles.title: Respiratory drug delivery: physiological, technical, and regulatory considerations for dissolution testing of orally inhaled dry powder aerosols.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pharmaceutical development of dry powder inhaler (DPI) products has traditionally relied on aerodynamic performance metrics. However, these parameters do not capture the post-deposition fate of inhaled particles, where dissolution impacts mucociliary clearance, macrophage uptake, retention and systemic absorption, particularly for poorly soluble drugs. Consequently, there is increasing interest in understanding the dissolution behavior of orally inhaled drug products. AREAS COVERED: This review critically examines the unique physiological environment of the lungs and the interactions of inhaled drugs with surfactants and mucins, highlighting why the respiratory tract cannot be regarded as a miniaturized gastrointestinal tract. It also discusses the dynamic interplay between dissolution and pulmonary clearance, alongside key methodological challenges in dissolution testing, including sample collection, apparatus design, dissolution media, and data analysis. Literature published between 1968 and 2026 was identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar and Web of Science databases. EXPERT OPINION: Widespread implementation of dissolution testing is hindered by the lack of standardized methodologies on aerosol collection, dissolution apparatuses, hydrodynamic conditions, and physiologically relevant dissolution media that can accurately replicate the lung environment. Future progress will require harmonized regulatory guidance, validated testing platforms for routine quality control and advanced biorelevant airway models for in vitro-in vivo relationship.

articles.title: Emerging therapeutic role of cinnamic acid derivatives in hyperuricemia and gout: mechanistic, translational, and pharmacological perspectives.
articles.abstract: Hyperuricemia and gout are increasingly common metabolic and inflammatory disorders characterized by excessive accumulation of uric acid, impaired urate excretion, oxidative stress, and monosodium urate crystal inflammation. Although currently available therapies such as xanthine oxidase inhibitors and uricosuric agents effectively reduce serum levels of uric acid, their long-term clinical use is often associated with adverse reactions, limited tolerability, and incomplete disease management. As a result, there is increasing interest in identifying natural compounds that may serve as a potential preclinical lead for the development of more targeted urate-lowering strategies. Cinnamic acid derivatives, including p-coumaric acid, caffeic acid, ferulic acid, sinapic acid, chlorogenic acid, and synthetic analogs such as 4-nitrocinnamic acid, have shown promising anti-hyperuricemic and anti-gout activities in experimental studies. These compounds have pharmacological effects through several mechanisms, including the inhibition of xanthine oxidase; modulation of urate transporters such as URAT1, GLUT9, and ABCG2; suppression of inflammatory pathways including NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome signalling; antioxidant activity; and protection against renal injuries induced by uric acid. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms, pharmacological evidence, and structure-activity relationships of selected cinnamic acid derivatives related to hyperuricemia and gout management. In addition, it discusses translational challenges associated with bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, toxicity evaluation, and clinical validation. Collectively, cinnamic acid derivatives represent promising pre-clinical leads that warrant further preclinical and clinical investigations to develop safer and more effective therapies against hyperuricemia and gout.

articles.title: Retraction Note: Protective effects of hesperidin against MTX-induced hepatotoxicity in male albino rats.
Redefining minoxidil therapy for androgenetic alopecia: from advanced drug delivery to precision treatment.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Minoxidil remains a cornerstone of pharmacological therapy for androgenetic alopecia (AGA), yet conventional topical formulations are constrained by pharmaceutical, biological, and patient-related limitations that compromise their real-world efficacy. Meanwhile, the rapid adoption of low-dose oral minoxidil (LDOM) is reshaping the therapeutic landscape and challenging the traditional paradigm of topical drug delivery. AREAS COVERED: This Perspective critically examines the limitations of conventional topical minoxidil, recent advances in topical drug-delivery technologies, and the resurgence of LDOM, including emerging clinical evidence and ongoing development programs. Pharmaceutical innovations aimed at optimizing oral therapy, including individualized dosing, alternative administration routes, personalized manufacturing, and combination strategies, are also discussed. Expert opinion: Future innovation should move beyond the pursuit of a universally superior minoxidil formulation toward matching the appropriate route, formulation, dose, and therapeutic strategy to individual patients. Rather than competing alternatives, topical and oral minoxidil may become complementary components of a precision-treatment framework integrating pharmaceutical technology, predictive biomarkers, pharmacogenetics, artificial intelligence, and digital health. We propose that this transition toward precision minoxidil therapy may define the next generation of AGA management.

articles.title: Absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion of londamocitinib after single-dose inhaled, intravenous and oral administration in healthy participants.
articles.abstract: AIM: Londamocitinib (AZD4604) is an inhaled, selective Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) inhibitor in development for asthma. This open-label, two-part, phase I clinical study (NCT06157255) used a radiolabelled microtracer approach to evaluate the absolute bioavailability and the absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME) of inhaled londamocitinib after intravenous and oral administration in healthy male and female participants (n = 8). METHODS: Pharmacokinetics, safety, metabolic profile and metabolite identification from plasma, urine, and faecal samples were assessed employing highly sensitive accelerator mass spectrometry. Participants received a single oral 4-mg dose of [14C]londamocitinib (NMT 37.0 kBq [14C]) in Part 1 and an intravenous 30-μg dose of [14C]londamocitinib (NMT 37.0 kBq [14C]), followed by a single inhaled dose of 3-mg londamocitinib in Part 2. RESULTS: Mean recovery of total radioactive material after oral dosing was 76.3% in faeces and 8.7% in urine. After intravenous dosing, recovery was 67.3% in faeces and 16.0% in urine. Absolute bioavailability of oral londamocitinib was 40.4% and for inhaled administration was 62.5%. Unchanged londamocitinib constituted approximately 70% of circulating radioactivity in plasma and accounted for 47.8% and 28.4% of the administered dose in excreta after oral and intravenous administration respectively. No new safety signals were observed. CONCLUSION: Following inhaled and oral dosing, londamocitinib demonstrated rapid absorption, and faecal excretion as the principal route of elimination. Unchanged londamocitinib and metabolite M6 were the major entities present in plasma, urine and faeces. Londamocitinib, at these doses, exhibited an acceptable safety and tolerability profile.

articles.title: Phase 1, open-label, randomized study of the elecoglipron pharmacokinetic profile in healthy participants under fed and fasted conditions.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Elecoglipron (AZD5004/ECC5004) is an oral small-molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1 RA) in development for weight management in people living with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes. This study aimed to characterize the pharmacokinetics (PK) profiles of two formulations of elecoglipron under fed and fasted conditions. METHODS: We assessed the PK profiles, safety and tolerability of two formulations of elecoglipron, 50 mg, under fed and fasted conditions in healthy participants in a phase 1, open-label, randomized, single-dose, fixed-sequence, crossover study. RESULTS: Of 23 participants screened, 14 were randomized to elecoglipron and 13 (92.9%) completed the study. The half-life for both formulations under fasted and fed conditions ranged between 20.7 and 21.2 h. Between the fed (reference) and fasted groups, geometric mean ratios (GMR) and 90% confidence intervals (CI) for the F1 formulation: area under the plasma-concentration curve (AUC) from time zero to the last measurement (AUC0-last) was 0.96 (0.82, 1.12), AUC from time zero extrapolated to infinity (AUC0-inf) was 0.95 (0.82, 1.11), and maximum plasma concentration (Cmax) was 1.15 (0.90, 1.46). Similar results were observed for F2 in the fed and fasted groups. Safety and tolerability were comparable for the two formulations. The most common AEs were gastrointestinal (nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, abdominal discomfort) and mostly mild in severity. CONCLUSIONS: Elecoglipron demonstrated a PK profile supportive of once-daily dosing and may be administered under fed or fasted conditions. These findings support the continuing clinical development of elecoglipron. The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06268145). The trial was first registered on 20 February 2024.

articles.title: Tongsai Granules Ameliorate Airway Mucus Hypersecretion in AECOPD by Remodeling LIPA-Driven Ceramide Metabolism.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Tongsai Granules (TSG) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula traditionally used for the treatment of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) with phlegm-heat obstructing lung syndrome, a condition characterized by cough, excessive sputum production, and dyspnea; however, its underlying therapeutic mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the mechanisms by which TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD through regulation of the LIPA/ceramide axis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A murine AECOPD model and airway epithelial cells were used. Proteomic and lipidomic analyses, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and LIPA overexpression and knockdown assays were performed. RESULTS: TSG improved pulmonary function, attenuated lung injury and inflammation, and suppressed MUC5AC expression in AECOPD mice. Multi-omics analyses showed that TSG regulated lipid metabolism and reduced triglyceride and ceramide accumulation while downregulating lysosomal acid lipase A (LIPA). Several serum-exposed constituents of TSG inhibited MUC5AC expression. Bergenin (BER) was selected as a representative bioactive constituent for subsequent target-identification and mechanistic studies. Molecular docking, SPR, and DARTS assays demonstrated direct interaction between BER and LIPA. LIPA knockdown suppressed MUC5AC expression, whereas LIPA overexpression attenuated the inhibitory effect of BER. Moreover, exogenous ceramide reversed BER-mediated suppression of MUC5AC. CONCLUSION: TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD by targeting the LIPA/ceramide axis. Bergenin directly targets LIPA to regulate lipid metabolism and suppress MUC5AC overexpression.

articles.title: CircPDS5B knockdown attenuates sevoflurane-induced developmental neurotoxicity and associated intracellular alkalinization.
articles.abstract: Neonatal sevoflurane exposure can cause developmental neurotoxicity, but the molecular events linking anesthetic exposure to neuronal injury remain incompletely understood. We examined whether circPDS5B-associated disruption of intracellular acid-base homeostasis contributes to this injury. Primary hippocampal neurons and postnatal day 5 (P5) rats were exposed to 4.0% sevoflurane for 6 h. Cultured neurons were transduced with adenovirus on day 4 in vitro (DIV 4), and neonatal rats received bilateral microinjections of Ad-sh-circPDS5B into hippocampal CA1 at P3. In vitro, sevoflurane increased circPDS5B expression, reduced miR-92a-3p and carbonic anhydrase IX (CA9) levels, and induced intracellular alkalinization, reduced viability, and organelle ultrastructural abnormalities. Dual-luciferase assays supported a sequence-specific interaction between circPDS5B and miR-92a-3p. CircPDS5B knockdown increased miR-92a-3p and CA9 expression toward control levels, attenuated intracellular alkalinization, and was associated with less prominent mitochondrial and endoplasmic reticulum ultrastructural abnormalities. In vivo, circPDS5B knockdown attenuated the sevoflurane-associated reductions in hippocampal CA9 expression and CA1 dendritic spine density and was associated with improved subsequent behavioral performance in the Morris water maze and open-field test. These findings support an association between circPDS5B dysregulation, altered intracellular pH regulation, and sevoflurane-induced developmental neurotoxicity. The circPDS5B/miR-92a-3p/CA9 axis should be considered a candidate regulatory mechanism pending pathway-specific rescue experiments.

articles.title: Role and mechanism of ATF6-mediated endoplasmic reticulum stress in ITLN-1 against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Intelectin-1 (ITLN-1), a novel adipocytokine, exerts neuroprotective effects against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), yet its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study focused on activating transcription factor 6 (ATF6), a key endoplasmic reticulum stress sensor, to explore its role in CIRI-induced neuronal injury and determine whether ITLN-1 mediates neuroprotection through ATF6 regulation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We established an N2a cell hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) model and a mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model. Using protein molecular docking, situ proximity ligation assay, Western blotting, mitochondrial membrane potential assays, and TUNEL staining, we investigated ATF6 activation in neuronal apoptosis and its upstream regulatory mechanisms. KEY FINDINGS: H/R injury markedly induced ATF6 activation in N2a cells, triggering mitochondrial dysfunction and promoting apoptosis. ATF6 overexpression further aggravated these effects, confirming its critical pathogenic role in CIRI. Mechanistic analyses revealed that ITLN-1 physically associates with ATF6. Both ITLN-1 overexpression and exogenous recombinant ITLN-1 administration significantly suppressed excessive ATF6 activation, modulated the JNK signaling pathway, improved cell viability, reduced intracellular calcium overload and reactive oxygen species accumulation, and attenuated neuronal apoptosis. In vivo, ITLN-1 ameliorated neurological deficits, reduced neuronal damage, and alleviated demyelination, whereas ITLN-1 knockdown produced opposite effects. SIGNIFICANCE: Excessive ATF6 activation underlies CIRI-induced neuronal injury. ITLN-1 exerts neuroprotection by inhibiting ATF6 and modulating JNK signaling, thereby alleviating mitochondrial dysfunction and reducing apoptosis. These findings highlight the ITLN-1/ATF6 axis as a promising therapeutic target for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Minimal essentials for humanized vessel-on-a-chip model for vascular research.
articles.abstract: AIMS: During the last decade, in vitro 3D models based on organ-on-a-chip technology have been developed, representing a biotechnology research advance towards more physiologically relevant models that aim to provide more predictable and less costly preclinical models. We aimed to develop a vessel-on-a-chip using a biocompatible microfluidic device co-cultured with human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: VSMC and HUVEC were isolated from umbilical cords and co-cultured in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) chip using specific growth media and tropoelastin-enriched media to favour extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis, which was measured by gene expression (quantitative polymerase chain reaction) and deposition (immunofluorescence), to establish an organized structure. Then, using a microfluidic pump system, the functional relevance of the model was evaluated by fluidic and permeability studies after a 9-day- cell growth period. KEY FINDINGS: Our vessel-on-a-chip model showed a bilayer structure, cell specific morphology and biomarkers phenotypes, and cell integrity. Gene and protein expression demonstrated the presence of ECM components, providing structural support and microenvironment control. It was observed that shear stress closer to the physiological range provided stability to the model and control of the permeability function. SIGNIFICANCE: Our 3D model may serve as a promising preclinical research tool that closely mimics the structural conformation of blood vessels and reflects essential physiological parameters, including cell maturity, shear stress, and functional permeability. Consequently, it could potentially be applied to cellular and molecular research to further elucidate vascular biology in cardiovascular diseases.

articles.title: PVA swelling microneedle (PVA-SMNs)-assisted enhancement of tacrolimus ointment penetration for improved psoriasis treatment.
articles.abstract: Psoriasis is a common chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease characterized by erythema and scaling, which imposes significant physical and psychological burdens on affected individuals. For facial psoriasis, clinical guidelines recommend tacrolimus (TAC) as an alternative to corticosteroid drugs due to its comparable efficacy and lower risk of adverse effects. However, in severe cases, the excessive proliferation of the stratum corneum leads to thick scales that significantly impede TAC permeation when the ointment is applied directly, resulting in unsatisfactory clinical outcomes. In this study, we propose a combination therapy involving pretreatment with swelling polyvinyl alcohol microneedles (PVA-SMNs) to create microchannels in the skin, followed by TAC ointment application. In vitro permeation tests (IVPT) revealed that PVA-SMNs enhanced the cumulative permeation of TAC by 2.7-fold. Pharmacodynamic studies further demonstrated that this approach significantly reduced the levels of key pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-17A, IL-23, and TNF-α), which are closely associated with psoriasis pathogenesis. Clinical trials corroborated these findings, providing direct evidence of the efficacy of PVA-SMN-assisted TAC delivery in improving psoriasis treatment. These promising results highlight the potential of this novel combination strategy, which may offer better therapeutic outcomes for psoriasis patients.

articles.title: Development of stereolithography 3D printed hollow vaginal devices with pore modulation to tailor the drug release.
articles.abstract: Vaginal infections affect nearly 70% of women worldwide at least once in their lifetime, yet conventional therapies remain suboptimal due to short residence time, leakage, and poor patient adherence. Long-acting vaginal systems such as rings and inserts can prolong drug release but are often limited by formulation constraints and the inability to accommodate diverse therapeutic agents. To address these challenges, we developed a novel hollow vaginal device fabricated via stereolithography (SLA) 3D printing using a biocompatible elastic resin. The C-shaped device features two precisely engineered pore openings that enable controlled drug release. Devices with pore diameters ranging from 0.5-2.0 mm were fabricated and loaded with a clindamycin phosphate aqueous gel, a first-line therapy for bacterial vaginosis. Drug release was modulated by the pore diameter and, at a fixed pore diameter, by the gel viscosity, enabling the dose to be adjusted. Mechanical testing confirmed that the elastic structure withstands repeated compression without deformation, ensuring mechanical robustness during vaginal retention. This versatile and customizable platform enables controlled and sustained intravaginal delivery of a wide range of therapeutics, representing a significant step toward patient-centric, next-generation vaginal drug delivery systems.

articles.title: Subcutaneous mesoporous silica formulation modulates systemic and tumor-associated paclitaxel exposure in a B16F10 melanoma model.
articles.abstract: Paclitaxel, a widely used chemotherapeutic agent for solid tumors, is primarily administered by intravenous infusion. Although subcutaneous administration has been investigated as a patient-centered alternative, developing subcutaneous paclitaxel formulations remains challenging. In this study, a mesoporous silica nanoparticle-based formulation (PCT112) containing paclitaxel, curcumin, and D-α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate was developed to modulate systemic and tumor-associated drug exposure after subcutaneous administration. PCT112 showed high encapsulation efficiencies for paclitaxel and curcumin and enabled amorphous drug incorporation within the silica matrix, resulting in sustained release and an increased paclitaxel solubility. In B16F10 melanoma cells, PCT112 showed time-dependent cytotoxicity, increased spheroid uptake, a delayed increase in apoptosis, and more pronounced microtubule disruption than free paclitaxel. In 3-dimensional multicellular tumor spheroids, higher Uptake Index values were associated with greater inhibition of spheroid growth. In B16F10 tumor-bearing mice, repeated subcutaneous administration of PCT112 produced dose-dependent tumor growth suppression and prolonged survival. Pharmacokinetic analysis showed delayed absorption and extended systemic exposure, whereas biodistribution analysis revealed dose-dependent increases in tumor-associated paclitaxel concentrations, which remained detectable over the observation period. Compared with intravenous Abraxane, longitudinal tumor-growth trajectories differed over time, while no statistically significant difference was observed at the final treatment day. Body-weight trajectories differed between the two groups. Collectively, these findings suggest that mesoporous silica-mediated subcutaneous delivery may support a lower-peak, prolonged exposure profile while increasing tumor-associated drug exposure, warranting further preclinical investigation for hydrophobic anticancer agents such as paclitaxel.

articles.title: Development and clinical evaluation of a palatable calcium acetate gummy formulation for patients undergoing hemodialysis.
articles.abstract: Phosphate binder therapy is essential for managing hyperphosphatemia in patients undergoing hemodialysis. However, nonadherence remains a common challenge. Gummy formulations are considered patient-friendly because they do not require water and are easily chewed. In this study, we developed a calcium acetate gummy formulation (CA-G) and evaluated its pharmaceutical properties and palatability in both healthy volunteers and patients undergoing hemodialysis. CA-G (3.5 g per formulation) was prepared using a gelatin-based matrix containing calcium acetate (CA; 250 mg) and organoleptic masking agents (flavors and sweeteners). The formulation was evaluated for drug content, dissolution behavior, water activity, penetration distance, and phosphate-binding efficacy. Four flavored CA-Gs (yuzu, Darjeeling tea, lemon, and apple) were prepared. In a gustatory sensation test, 24 healthy volunteers evaluated palatability using a 100-mm visual analog scale (VAS). In addition, palatability was assessed by nine patients undergoing hemodialysis using a 5-point scale, and changes in serum phosphate levels were explored. CA content was 102.8% of the intended amount; maximum dissolution rate was 97.6%; water activity was 0.732; and penetration distance was 13.1 mm. Incorporation of CA into the gummy matrix did not compromise maximum phosphate-binding efficacy. Flavored CA-Gs showed significantly higher palatability VAS scores than the non-flavored formulation in healthy volunteers, with at least 75% of patients rating them acceptable. Serum phosphate levels decreased after CA-G supplementation. These findings suggest that palatable and flavor-varied CA-G may represent a patient-friendly dosage-form option for patients undergoing hemodialysis.

articles.title: A dimensionless framework for hold-up mass prediction and scale transfer in continuous linear blending.
articles.abstract: In this work, a dimensionless model is proposed to describe the influence of operating conditions on the hold-up mass (HUM) of a continuous linear blender. The model relates the fill level (normalized hold‑up mass per blender volume) to three key dimensionless groups: a flow-related parameter (χ), the Froude number (Fr), and the number of mixing elements (H). A physically interpretable analytical expression is introduced and calibrated using experimental data across multiple materials and operating conditions. The model demonstrates strong predictive performance, with root mean square errors typically below 5%. Predictions obtained with the intermediate shaft configuration, which was excluded from parameter calibration, demonstrated the model's interpolation capability and calibration robustness. Furthermore, scale transfer was evaluated by calibrating the model using a smaller scale CDC-10 blender and applying it to predict fill level in a larger CDC-50 blender. Comparable prediction errors between calibration and external validation demonstrate the ability of the model to capture the dominant trends governing hold-up behavior across the process conditions studied. In addition, a simplified set of scale transfer rules is derived from the dimensionless framework, showing that maintaining Froude number and χ enables consistent performance across scales. These rules are experimentally validated across a range of formulations and operating conditions, including a real industrial case study. Overall, this work provides a predictive framework to quantify and transfer blending conditions in continuous tableting, supporting more efficient process development and more robust scale transfer.

articles.title: Triphenyl phosphate may reduced oxidative muscle-fiber phenotype involving IL-17A-p38 MAPK -PGC1- α signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: TPHP is widely used in various fields. In recent years, the potential health hazards of this pollutant have attracted great attention from people. However, the impact and potential mechanisms of TPHP on skeletal muscle function still need to be studied. METHODS: This study combined in vivo animal and in vitro cell experiments. Thirty C57BL/6J mice were randomly assigned to CON, T25, and T50 groups and received 8-week TPHP gavage treatment. Gastrocnemius tissues were collected for transcriptome sequencing, qPCR, Western blotting (WB), and immunofluorescence (IF) analyses. In vitro, C2C12 myoblasts were exposed to gradient TPHP concentrations for 24 h and subjected to identical molecular detections. RESULTS: This study showed that after intervention with TPHP, muscle atrophy markers increased in the gastrocnemius muscle of mice( p < 0.05 for T25; p < 0.01 for T50), while the expression of genes and proteins related to oxidative muscle fibers decreased( p < 0.05 for T25; p < 0.01 for T50). Gene sequencing results showed an increase in IL-17A pathway expression. Cell experiments also showed that after TPHP intervention, the expression of genes and proteins related to muscle atrophy increased in cells ( p < 0.05 for T25; p < 0.01 for T50), while the expression of genes and proteins related to oxidative muscle fibers decreased( p < 0.05 for T25; p < 0.01 for T50). By using relevant inhibitors, provides validation that the IL-17A -p38 MAPK-PGC1-α pathway can reduce oxidative muscle -fiber phenotype. CONCLUSIONS: Our research findings indicate that TPHP may reduced oxidative muscle-fiber phenotype involving IL-17A-p38 MAPK-PGC1-α signaling pathway.

articles.title: Subanesthetic ketamine modulates region-specific neural and endocrine responses to acute stress in rats.
articles.abstract: Exposure to acute, inescapable stress triggers a coordinated neural and endocrine response across corticolimbic and brainstem circuits. Although subanesthetic ketamine has rapid antidepressant effects, it is unclear whether its modulation of the stress-response network depends on the presence of an acute stressor. In this study, naïve rats received subanesthetic ketamine (15 mg/kg) or a vehicle, and then underwent the tail suspension test (TST) or remained undisturbed in their home cages. Ketamine reduced immobility in the TST and attenuated the stress-induced increase in plasma corticosterone levels. Regional c-Fos expression, ascertained through quantitative real-time PCR and immunohistochemistry, revealed region-specific and context-dependent modulation. Ketamine selectively activated neuronal populations in the prefrontal cortex and potentiated stress-induced activation in the hippocampus and dorsal raphe nucleus. However, it suppressed stress-driven hyperactivation in the amygdala and elicited non-additive activation patterns in the brainstem. These findings suggest that subanesthetic ketamine modulates reconfigures the regional balance of neuronal activation and attenuates hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis reactivity in a state-dependent manner. Furthermore, its effects on the stress-response network are fundamentally influenced by the presence of an acute stressor.

articles.title: Population pharmacogenomics of CYP1A2, CYP2C19, CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 in a Uruguayan cohort with schizophrenia.
articles.abstract: Latin American populations remain underrepresented in pharmacogenomic research, limiting the applicability of genomic findings to these groups. Uruguay, with its unique admixed demographic history, constitutes a relevant case study for characterizing clinically significant pharmacogene variation. In this work, we characterized haplotypic diversity across four CYP450 genes, CYP1A2, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4, in a cohort of 47 Uruguayan patients with treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) receiving clozapine. Star-allele frequencies in the TRS cohort were contextualized against the Urugenomes Phase 2 dataset (U2; n = 30), used as the primary Uruguayan population reference, alongside two ancestry-enriched datasets comprising Indigenous-admixed (n = 10) and Afro-Uruguayan (n = 10) individuals. Star-allele and diplotype inference was performed using Aldy v4.8.3, and population-level frequencies were contextualized against global biogeographic references from PharmFreq and gnomAD. CYP1A2*30 predominated across all Uruguayan datasets, while CYP3A4 showed near-complete dominance of the *1 allele. CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 displayed greater inter-dataset heterogeneity, with metabolizer phenotype distributions differing from global reference populations. To assess the clinical relevance of this pharmacogenomic variation, multivariable linear regression models were constructed to predict plasma clozapine concentrations, incorporating clinical, behavioral, and genetic predictors. A model combining HDL, triglycerides, glycemia, cigarette consumption, and CYP1A2*30 allele count explained 41% of the variance in clozapine levels (adjusted R² = 0.41), representing a statistically significant improvement over the clinical-only model (ANOVA p = 0.034). Bootstrap resampling confirmed the stability of all estimated effects, and leave-one-out cross-validation yielded a corrected R² of 0.31. These findings contribute to characterizing the pharmacogenomic landscape of an underrepresented Latin American population and suggest that locally generated CYP haplotype data may complement clinical factors in explaining interindividual variability in clozapine exposure in this population.

articles.title: Virulence mechanisms of Desulfovibrio bacteria: viability-dependent processes promote alpha-synuclein aggregation and toxicity in C. elegans.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Desulfovibrio (DSV) species have been linked to Parkinson's disease (PD) and demonstrated to enhance alpha-synuclein (alpha-syn) aggregation, a pathological hallmark of PD, in a Caenorhabditis elegans model. However, the bacterial factors underlying this virulence remain unclear. We investigated whether DSV-induced alpha-syn aggregation and toxicity are more strongly driven by bacterial viability-dependent processes or by bacterial structures retained after paraformaldehyde (PFA) treatment. METHODS: Live or paraformaldehyde (PFA)-treated (non-viable) DSV cells, and curli-producing or curli-deficient E. coli as controls were fed to C. elegans. Worm survival, alpha-syn aggregation, hydrogen sulfide production, and expression of genes associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, proteostasis and dopaminergic function were evaluated. RESULTS: Curli-producing E. coli retained its ability to induce alpha-syn aggregation, whereas PFA-treated DSV strains lost this effect, showing reduced aggregate number and volume (P < 0.05). Worm survival improved when fed PFA-treated cells, although the difference was not statistically significant. Expression of pmk-1, skn-1 and hsf-1 did not differ between worms fed live and PFA-treated DSV bacteria, while cat-2 expression increased in worms fed PFA-treated bacteria compared to those fed live cells. Patient-derived DSV strains produced substantially higher levels of H2S than healthy control strains (1058.11 vs. 710.30 ppm/OD600; P = 0.003), and H2S levels were positively correlated with aggregate volume (Spearman's rs = 0.886, P = 0.019). CONCLUSIONS: DSV-derived viability-dependent processes, including metabolic activity, more strongly promote alpha-syn aggregation and toxicity than structural components. These findings highlight the important contribution of bacterial viability-dependent processes to DSV-mediated pathogenic effects relevant to Parkinson's disease.

articles.title: Rosmarinic acid- and epigallocatechin gallate-enriched extracts improve insomnia and sleep-wake balance in caffeine-and p-chlorophenylalanine-induced insomnia models.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the effects of a rosmarinic acid- and epigallocatechin gallate-enriched extract mixture (RE-GTE) on insomnia and sleep-wake disturbances induced by excessive caffeine intake or serotonin depletion using p-chlorophenylalanine (PCPA) in mice. RE-GTE was administered in both caffeine- and PCPA-induced insomnia models, and sleep-related behaviors were assessed using pentobarbital-induced sleep tests and behavioral analyses of anxiety-related and locomotor parameters. In addition, sleep-related neurotransmitters and receptor expression were examined using molecular and biochemical approaches. In the caffeine-induced insomnia model, RE-GTE supplementation significantly attenuated caffeine-induced dopaminergic hyperactivity, increased gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) levels, and improved anxiety-related and selected locomotor behavioral parameters. RE-GTE also upregulated GABAA receptor expression while reducing adenosine A1 and A2A receptor expression, accompanied by increased sleep duration. In the PCPA-induced insomnia model, RE-GTE increased hypothalamic serotonin and melatonin levels, reduced stress-related hormones including adrenocorticotropic hormone and corticosterone, increased serotonin receptor expression, and reduced overexpression of the orexin 2 receptor, indicating selective modulation of serotonergic and stress-related markers. Across both models, high-dose RE-GTE (40 mg/kg) increased sleep duration toward normal levels. Collectively, these findings indicate that RE-GTE ameliorates insomnia-related behavioral and neurochemical disturbances and that this improvement is accompanied by selective changes in adenosinergic, GABAergic, and serotonergic markers. These pathway-level associations support further investigation of RE-GTE as a promising natural candidate for the management of sleep disturbances.

articles.title: Dorsomedial striatum calcium permeable AMPA receptors in the development of aversion-resistant alcohol drinking.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Alcohol use disorder is defined by drinking alcohol despite knowledge of negative consequences, often referred to as aversion-resistant drinking (The dorsomedial (DMS) and dorsolateral striatum (DLS) are necessary for goal-directed and habitual action selection, respectively. Leading hypotheses posit that once drug use becomes compulsive, DMS dependence degrades while DLS dependence increases. This shift may be mediated by changes in synaptic weights from glutamatergic inputs. OBJECTIVES: Using a combination of western-blot, micro-injections, and ex-vivo electrophysiology in male and female C57BL/6J mice, we investigated the role of α-Amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptors AMPAR, which drive glutamatergic transmission, during quinine-adulterated alcohol drinking in the DMS and DLS across the development of aversion-resistant drinking. RESULTS: We found that AMPAR subunit composition and function change in the DMS across the development of aversion-resistant drinking whereby, calcium permeable (CP) - AMPARs drive behavior. Western blots revealed a negative relationship between DMS GluA1 and quinine-adulterated alcohol drinking in alcohol naive mice and a positive relationship between DMS Glu A1/A2 ratios and quinine-adulterated alcohol drinking in aversion-resistant mice indicating that aversion-resistance positively predicts likelihood for CP-AMPAR expression in the DMS. Female aversion-resistant mice also had significant positive relationships with DMS or DLS Glu A1/A2 ratios and female aversion-resistant mice had a significant negative relationship with GluA2 and aversion-resistant alcohol drinking. DMS CP-AMPAR antagonism caused an increase in quinine-adulterated alcohol drinking in alcohol naïve mice suggesting that CP-AMPARs in the DMS prevent aversion-resistant drinking. Ex-vivo electrophysiology of DMS spiny projection neurons revealed that aversion-resistant drinking mice had greater inward rectification and CP-AMPAR antagonist sensitivity than alcohol naïve mice indicating that spiny projection neurons in the DMS express more CP-AMPARs following the development of aversion-resistant drinking. However, sensitivity to CP-AMPAR antagonism negatively predicted aversion-resistant drinking in alcohol history mice. CONCLUSIONS: These data provide evidence that repeated alcohol binges alter DMS CP-AMPAR activity, where initial DMS activity acts to causally prevent aversion-resistant drinking but after repeated binges that result in aversion-resistant alcohol drinking, DMS spiny projection neurons recruit CP-AMPARs. CP-AMPAR antagonism was negatively association with aversion-resistant drinking within the alcohol history mice suggesting that plasticity of DMS CP-AMPARs is not related to quinine-sensitivity. These data provide evidence for a causal role of the DMS in aversion-resistant drinking and open questions as to the functional role of CP-AMPARs across the drinking history and striatal cell types.

articles.title: Gastrodin alleviates acute colitis with comorbid anxiety- and depression-like behaviours rather than cognitive dysfunction by modulating gut microbiota and suppressing inflammation.
articles.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) patients frequently suffer from emotional disturbances, predominantly anxiety- and depression-like symptoms, and may also have cognitive dysfunction, but the mechanisms remain unclear, and no therapies targeting the gut or nervous system exist. Gastrodin (GAS), the primary active component of Gastrodia elata, has anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective effects. Whether GAS can alleviate acute colitis with comorbid anxiety- and depression-like behaviours or cognitive dysfunction via the gut-brain axis is unknown. Using a 3% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse model, we administered GAS (240 mg/kg) by gavage for 7 days. The open field, elevated plus maze, tail suspension, and forced swimming tests showed that GAS improved behavioural abnormalities (including anxiety- and depression-like behaviours); it also restored colon length and reduced colonic histopathological injury. Metagenomic sequencing revealed that GAS reshaped the gut microbiota, increasing Sporosarcina and Nitrospirae while decreasing Clostridiaceae and Lachnospiraceae. Untargeted metabolomics indicated that GAS shifted the metabolic profile away from DSS and normalized taurine levels, and KEGG pathway analysis suggested that GAS may partially ameliorate DSS-induced metabolic disturbances by downregulating virulence-related pathways and upregulating energy metabolic pathways such as the TCA cycle and oxidative phosphorylation relative to DSS. Western blot confirmed that GAS restored the tight junction protein Occludin and decreased TNF-α. Quantitative proteomics demonstrated that GAS reversed the aberrant expression of 191 colonic proteins. These results demonstrate correlative associations between GAS treatment and the alleviation of acute colitis and behavioural abnormalities, alongside concurrent changes in gut microbiota composition, metabolite profiles, and intestinal barrier proteins. Whether these associations reflect a causal gut-brain axis mechanism requires direct experimental validation. GAS modulates the microbiota, partially restores metabolism, repairs the gut barrier, and suppresses local inflammation, suggesting a potential gut-brain axis mechanism. These findings position GAS as a promising candidate for further mechanistic and translational investigation in IBD-associated behavioural comorbidities.

articles.title: Melatonin nanoemulgel for dermal applications: from formulation to in vivo imaging validation.
articles.abstract: Radiation-induced dermatitis is a prevalent side effect of radiotherapy worldwide. Conventional treatment strategies often fall short of achieving optimal therapeutic efficacy, primarily due to inadequate retention on the skin surface. This limitation has motivated research to find new nanotechnology-based treatment approaches to enhance therapeutic outcomes. Nanoformulations have emerged as a promising solution, offering improved therapeutic outcomes. In this study, authors investigated a combination therapy consisting of melatonin (MLT), vitamin E (VE), and N-acetyl cysteine (NAC). MLT is a naturally occurring hormone that has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties that may help treat cancer. It plays a crucial part in protecting healthy tissues by neutralizing various free radical scavengers generated by IR pro-oxidant enzymes that are triggered after exposure to IR. VE and NAC also depict radiomitigator properties. In the present study, nanoemulgel was formulated with Carbopol®940, which acts as a gelatinizing agent to facilitate effective delivery of these therapeutic agents at the target site. Pseudoternary phase diagrams were prepared to classify the area of nanoemulsion region. Globule size and zeta potential of optimized nanoemulsion formulation were observed to be 113.84 ± 0.648 nm and 34.2 ± 0.907 mV, respectively. Further, in vitro skin release studies showed 49.94 ± 3.01% cumulative release of MLT from nanoemulgel a time frame of 24 h. And the formulation followed Korsmeyer-Peppas model, which indicates that drug release is non-fickian. An FTIR analysis confirmed that MLT's characteristic peaks were preserved in the formulations, demonstrating that no interaction occurred between the constituents. The DSC thermogram of MLT nanoemulgel showed no sharp melting peak, suggesting molecular dispersion in oil phase. Additionally, gamma scintigraphy evaluation confirmed the formulation's long-term skin retention. In experimental results, nanoemulsion gel showed enhanced permeability and retention, making it a promising transporter for topical deliveries of bioactives for radiation-induced dermatitis prevention.

articles.title: Evaluation of antiseptic drug candidate pyridosept in preclinical in vivo toxicity studies.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study is to assess the safety profile of the antiseptic drug candidate pyridosept in preclinical in vivo toxicity tests. The safety of pyridosept was assessed in acute toxicity tests in rats, mice and rabbits via dermal, intragastric, intraperitoneal, and inhalation routes of administration. Subchronic dermal toxicity of pyridosept was evaluated following cutaneous application for 90 days in rats and rabbits. Pyridosept was also examined in the accumulation test in rats and in micronucleus assay in the skin and bone marrow of mice after single and repeated administration. Acute oral toxicity study of pyridosept revealed an LD50 of 1208 mg/kg in mice and 1242 mg/kg in rats, a dermal LD50 > 2000 mg/kg in both species, and an LD50 of 23-32 mg/kg upon intraperitoneal administration. In the 90-day dermal toxicity study in rats, no systemic toxicity was found; the only treatment-related effects were reversible local skin reactions at intermediate and high doses. In the 90-day rabbit study, dermatitis, granulomatous hepatitis, and mild interstitial nephritis occurred; however, the incidence of hepatitis did not differ significantly from the control and showed no dose dependence. In the skin accumulation study, the cumulation coefficient (Kk = 12.8) indicated no cumulative properties, and the micronucleus assay demonstrated no mutagenic activity in mouse skin or bone marrow. Pyridosept's acute toxicity upon oral administration is more favorable than that of benzalkonium chloride, comparable to miramistin, and slightly less favorable than chlorhexidine. The results of in vivo pharmacokinetic, allergenic, and immunotoxicity studies of pyridosept will be presented in forthcoming publications.

articles.title: Investigation of the pharmacological and circuit basis for psychedelic drug effects on interval timing in mice.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Classical psychedelic drugs such as the tryptamine psilocybin can alter temporal perception. Previously, the phenylethylamine psychedelic 2,5-dimethoxy-4-iodoamphetamine (DOI), a 5-HT2A receptor agonist, altered timing precision and accuracy in mice performing the discrete-trials temporal discrimination task (TDT), a retrospective timing task where subjects differentially respond depending on whether a light is illuminated for shorter or longer than 6.5 s. OBJECTIVES: Although DOI alters TDT performance, it is unclear whether timing is altered by tryptamine psychedelics, which are less selective for 5-HT2 subtypes and also activate the 5-HT1A receptor. METHODS: To address this knowledge gap, we tested psilocin (the active metabolite of psilocybin) in male C57BL/6J mice performing the TDT and assessed the involvement of 5-HT1A and 5-HT2A receptors in its effects. Because the prefrontal cortex (PFC) is involved in psychedelic drug effects and temporal perception, additional experiments tested whether DOI microinfusion into the medial PFC (mPFC) replicates its systemic effects. RESULTS: Psilocin (0.8 mg/kg SC) altered timing accuracy and precision in mice performing the TDT, similarly to DOI. Psilocin effects were blocked by the 5-HT2A antagonist M100907 but were unaffected by the 5-HT1A antagonist WAY-100,635. Infusion of DOI bilaterally into mPFC mimicked the effect of systemic administration on TDT performance. Administration of the selective 5-HT2A inverse agonists M100907 and MDL 11,939 altered timing accuracy, demonstrating that both increases and reductions in 5-HT2A receptor activation can modulate perceived clock speed. CONCLUSIONS: The mPFC appears to play a role in TDT performance and may mediate the effects of psychedelic drugs on interval timing.

articles.title: Meropenem Exposure, Target Attainment, and Therapeutic Drug Monitoring Practices in Critically Ill Adults Receiving Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To critically evaluate meropenem pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) target attainment, therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), infusion strategies, and clinical outcomes during continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). DATA SOURCES: Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to August 15, 2026, using meropenem, TDM, β-lactam, and CRRT terms, with adult, human, and English-language limits. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Thirteen reports representing 12 unique studies (2 randomized, 10 non-randomized) reporting meropenem concentration data during CRRT were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I. DATA SYNTHESIS: Total clearance ranged from 3.60 to 6.6 L/h. Lower or primary PK/PD target non-attainment ranged from 0% to 26.7%, while aggressive-target non-attainment ranged from 0% to 53.3% in most analyses and reached 93% in 1 study when a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 8 mg/L was assumed. Continuous or prolonged infusion may facilitate sustained exposure, but comparative evidence was limited. Four used routine TDM; only 2 implemented protocolized TDM-guided dose adjustment. Low exposure was associated with higher mortality in 1 adjusted observational analysis, but evidence for clinical outcomes was of very low certainty. RELEVANCE TO PATIENT CARE AND CLINICAL PRACTICE: Standardized meropenem regimens cannot be assumed to provide consistent exposure during CRRT. Optimized infusion and timely, protocolized TDM may support individualized dosing when multidisciplinary expertise is available. CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence supports a shift from standardized empirical dosing toward individualized, measurement-guided meropenem therapy in patients receiving CRRT.

articles.title: Association of bisphenol A exposure on hormone-associated benign and malignant disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Bisphenol A (BPA) and its analogs have garnered considerable public and scientific attention due to their endocrine-disrupting properties in humans. This systematic review aims to address the question of whether exposure to Bisphenol A is associated with the risk of hormone-associated benign and malignant disorders. METHODS: A comprehensive literature search was conducted from inception to February 2024 to identify eligible human case-control studies investigating exposure to BPA and its analogs. The study selection and data extraction processes were performed independently and in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. All analyses were conducted using Review Manager (RevMan) software, version 5.4. RESULTS: Following the removal of duplicate records, 661 eligible articles were identified, with 44 studies ultimately included in the final analysis. Bisphenol A was the most frequently investigated contaminant, whereas its analogs were only reported in one study. Most studies reported PCOS, breast cancers, benign and malignant endometrial disorders and only one study reported prostate cancer. The result indicate that BPA exposure is associated with PCOS (SMD=1.19; CI95: 0.70-1.67), benign endometrial disorders (SMD=0.94; CI95: 0.15, 1.73), breast cancer (SMD=0.68; CI95: 0.44-0.92). Nevertheless, these associations demonstrate considerable heterogeneity. CONCLUSION: Bisphenol A exposure is associated with the risk endocrine-related benign and malignant disorders, such as PCOS, breast cancer, and benign endometrial disorders. Nevertheless, the interpretation of these findings is limited by substantial heterogeneity, largely attributable to small sample sizes in case and control groups.

articles.title: Antifungal ototoxicity, itraconazole, and approaches to its mitigation: a review of a sparse evidence base.
articles.abstract: 1. INTRODUCTION: Hearing loss is a recognised hazard of aminoglycosides and platinum chemotherapy, but the auditory risk of antifungal drugs has received far less attention. Itraconazole lists hearing loss in its prescribing information, yet dedicated peer-reviewed auditory studies appear absent. 2. AREAS COVERED: The original 139-record Web of Science (WoS) title-only corpus was retained to map the wider ototoxicity field. A targeted WoS Topic-field sensitivity search using antifungal-specific terms and broader auditory outcomes retrieved 153 records, of which 18 direct antifungal auditory safety/toxicity studies were retained. No dedicated auditory study of itraconazole was identified. The expanded evidence shows formulation- and route-dependent topical effects, a pharmacovigilance signal for oral terbinafine, no auditory brainstem response shift in a short-duration animal study of systemic voriconazole or caspofungin, and rare hearing-loss reports plus a pharmacovigilance signal for amphotericin B. Otoprotection evidence from other drug classes is considered for transferable mitigation principles. 3. EXPERT OPINION: The broader search shows a heterogeneous but sparse evidence base rather than an absence of evidence. Human systemic azole data remain particularly limited, and itraconazole lacks dedicated auditory investigation. Baseline and serial audiometry, separation of drug effects from infection and interacting medicines, and mechanistic studies are priorities.

articles.title: Nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD-), leucine-rich repeat (LRR-), and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome and snake venoms/toxins: mechanisms, pathophysiological relevance, and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: Snake envenoming triggers a complex inflammatory response that substantially contributes to local tissue destruction and systemic complications. Among the innate immune pathways implicated in venom-induced injury, the nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain (NOD-), leucine-rich repeat (LRR-), and pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome has emerged as a key sensor-effector platform linking tissue damage, ionic imbalance, reactive oxygen species (ROS), lipid mediators, and cytokine maturation. Experimental studies indicate that crude venoms and isolated snake toxins, including Lys49 and Asp49 phospholipase A2 (PLA2), metalloproteinases, and C-type lectin/C-type lectin-like proteins, can activate NLRP3 inflammasome-dependent signaling, leading to caspase-1 activation, interleukin (IL)-1β release, and, in some settings, pyroptotic cell death. These findings position the NLRP3 inflammasome as a promising adjunctive therapeutic target in snakebite envenoming, although causal evidence remains restricted to selected toxin models and broader validation across venom classes is still required. This review summarizes the current understanding of NLRP3 inflammasome biology in the context of snake venoms and toxins, discusses the molecular mechanisms proposed for inflammasome priming and activation, and highlights unresolved questions relevant to toxinology, immunology, and adjunctive therapy development. Recent literature also places venom-derived molecules within the broader framework of NLRP3 inflammasome modulation, reinforcing the idea that venoms may serve both as drivers of pathology and as sources of pharmacological leads.

articles.title: Evaluation of Clinical Outcomes of Selective Versus Nonselective Beta-Blockers Among Patients With Heart Failure With Reduced Ejection Fraction Receiving Sacubitril/Valsartan.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Beta-blockers, selective (metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol) and nonselective (carvedilol), and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors (ARNIs) are the first-line guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Concomitant use of carvedilol and ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) may result in additive vasodilatory effects, which may increase the risk of hypotension and limit dose titration of sacubitril/valsartan. OBJECTIVE: This study examines differences in clinical endpoints between selective and nonselective beta-blocker therapy among patients with HFrEF receiving sacubitril/valsartan. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study utilized TriNetX Research Collaborative real-world data. Patients receiving sacubitril/valsartan concomitantly with carvedilol were identified as the intervention cohort, while those receiving metoprolol succinate or bisoprolol served as controls. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause mortality or all-cause hospitalization during the 3-year follow-up. Propensity score matching (PSM) balanced confounders. Kaplan-Meier analyses were used to estimate event-free survival, and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using Cox proportional hazards models for time-to-event outcomes. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the findings. RESULTS: Overall, 75 230 patients received carvedilol and 21 587 received metoprolol/bisoprolol. After PSM, 20 939 patients were included in each group. Carvedilol was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite endpoint compared with those taking metoprolol or bisoprolol (52.32% vs 46.29%; HR: 1.21; 95% CI, 1.17-1.24; P < .0001). Carvedilol was also linked to increased hospitalization risk (HR: 1.32; 95% CI, 1.28-1.36; P < .0001) but a modest reduction in mortality (HR: 0.92; 95% CI, 0.87-0.97; P = .0011). In addition, carvedilol was associated with higher risks of hypotension, end-stage renal disease, and bradycardia. Sensitivity analysis results were consistent for the primary endpoint. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Our results suggest that carvedilol may be associated with a higher risk of the composite endpoint, health care utilization, and adverse events but lower all-cause mortality compared with metoprolol or bisoprolol in patients with HFrEF taking sacubitril/valsartan.

articles.title: Design, In Silico Targeting, and Characterization of Curcumin-Ibuprofen Prodrug Microspheres for Brain-Specific Delivery in Alzheimer's Therapy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative condition characterized by limited treatment effectiveness, attributed to inadequate Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) permeability and low medication absorption. Curcumin and ibuprofen possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties but are limited by pharmacokinetic constraints. This study aimed to synthesize a curcumin-ibuprofen mutual prodrug (CIP), formulate it into chitosan-based microspheres (CIPM), and evaluate its neuroprotective potential for brain-targeted delivery in AD. METHODS: CIP was synthesized via ethylenediamine carbodiimide (EDCI) mediated esterification and confirmed through IR, NMR, LC-MS, and DSC. CIPM microspheres were prepared using emulsion crosslinking, characterized by scanning electron microscopy, drug entrapment efficiency (85.5%), zeta potential, particle size analysis, and DSC. In silico tools (SwissADME, ProTox-II) and molecular docking were used to assess ADMET profiles and target binding (AChE, BACE1, β-secretase). Network pharmacology identified overlapping targets between curcumin and AD. In vivo evaluation was conducted in a TMT (Trimethyltin)- induced neurodegeneration rat model through behavioral Morris Water Maze (MWM), Novel Object Recognition (NOR), Social Recognition Test (SRT), and biochemical and histological assessments. RESULTS: CIP demonstrated strong binding affinity with AD-related targets (-10.0 to -8.5 kcal/mol) and favorable ADMET properties.
